title: Native and Multiplatform Performance
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of native and multiplatform performance using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates native and multiplatform performance.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Native and Multiplatform Performance** as part of **Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, and Kotlin/Native**. Kotlin Multiplatform organizes shared logic and target-specific implementations through source sets; only APIs available for every configured target belong in common code. Use the subtopics—Platform-Specific Profiling, Native Binary Size, Cross-Platform Performance Trade-offs—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-platform targets differ in runtime APIs, toolchains, and support maturity. Check the current compatibility matrix before committing to a production target.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A source-code change is an optimization even without measurements.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
